items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: when you talk about real players, who my favorites was like Buddy Petit, Kid Punch, you know what I mean, Kid Punch? Well, I used to love him when I was a kid. Now, he was one of my real favorites.

ctx.x: Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

Oh, that's a kind of hard thing. Sure. To say, because you know the reason why, when I was a kid, you're talking about it? Yeah. Because I was listening to the cornet and trumpets all my, what's that cornet then, that damn night. All my days, I just loved it. My mother wouldn't buy me one. She wouldn't buy me a violin. I didn't want to buy me. But anyway, I had my, well, before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez. He had such a name around there, you know, around him. He, when…
I said, plenty gold on the lawn socks. No, I didn't know.

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: she had Kit René a lot, she had Punch, had Buddy Pt, to play for a different time.

ctx.x: Do you remember any of the parades or any other early bands or dance artisers when you were a kid?

Oh yes, in fact I remember practically, I should remember all of them because my aunt, her name, it's Kalis Dele, she was my father's oldest sister. She gave dances continuously. Oh, where did they give those dances? She used to give at the economy hall, at the cooperatives hall, the Jeanne Zami and the Franz Zami. She gave them many dances. Most of the old timers remember, but in those days, well I was a kid, although interested in music. Did you hear the music? Did you hear the dances too? Yes, yes, yes. You…
Mother's dances, and they weren't the organization, they gave it just the private party.
